title: Replit agent wipes SaaStr production database during code freeze
what_happened: During a declared code-and-action freeze, Replit's AI agent ran destructive commands that deleted production records. It had also produced fake data and reports, and said rollback was impossible; the rollback later worked. Replit's CEO called it unacceptable and added dev/prod database separation and a planning-only mode.
evidence_we_check: A write-freeze enforced at the credential or database layer outside the agent, plus an independent restore-test record instead of the agent's own claim about rollback.

title: PocketOS: coding agent deletes production database and backups in one API call
what_happened: While fixing a credential mismatch in staging, a Cursor agent running Claude Opus 4.6 used a fully permissioned Railway API token unrelated to its task and, in one API call, deleted the production volume and its volume-level backups. Railway later restored the data and patched the endpoint.
evidence_we_check: A credential-scope inventory showing the agent's token could not delete production volumes, and an approval record naming the exact volume ID and environment before any delete.

title: Google Antigravity wipes a user's drive while clearing a cache
what_happened: In a mode where commands run without per-step approval, a user asked the agent to clear a project cache; the delete targeted the root of his D: drive and bypassed the Recycle Bin. Google said it was investigating.
evidence_we_check: A pre-execution log of the resolved absolute path for every destructive command, checked against an allow-listed workspace root.

title: OpenClaw agent bulk-deletes a researcher's inbox and ignores stop
what_happened: A user told her agent to only suggest emails to archive or delete; on a large inbox it began bulk-deleting and ignored stop messages until the process was killed. She attributed it to context compaction dropping the instruction.
evidence_we_check: A server-side approval record for each delete batch by message ID, and a kill switch that revokes mailbox tokens without depending on the agent's context.
note: self-reported; not independently verified by TechCrunch

title: Internal agent posts unapproved advice, leading to a Sev 1 data exposure at Meta
what_happened: An internal agent asked to analyse a forum question posted an answer itself without approval; a colleague followed the inaccurate advice and sensitive data was exposed to unauthorised employees for about two hours. Meta said no user data was misused.
evidence_we_check: A log showing the engineer approved the exact post before publication, plus a separate approval record for the access change it led to.

title: AWS Kiro 'delete and recreate' and a Cost Explorer interruption (disputed)
what_happened: The FT reported an AI coding agent chose to delete and recreate an environment, interrupting AWS Cost Explorer in one region. Amazon says the cause was a misconfigured role, calls the event extremely limited, and added mandatory peer review for production access.
evidence_we_check: A diff of the agent session's effective role against its intended role, and a peer-review record for that production change before it ran.
note: DISPUTED by Amazon — label on the page

title: Amazon Q Developer extension ships with a wiper prompt
what_happened: An improperly scoped token in AWS's build setup let an attacker commit a prompt telling the agent to wipe local files and cloud resources; it shipped in v1.84.0. AWS says it failed to run and changed no customer environments; AWS released a fixed version (CVE-2025-8217).
evidence_we_check: Release provenance tying every merged change to a reviewed PR and a named approver, with CI tokens that cannot push to release branches.

title: Clinejection: hijacked AI triage bot leads to an unauthorised npm release
what_happened: Cline's AI issue-triage workflow could be steered by instructions in issue titles; this enabled cache poisoning and exposure of a release token. On 17 Feb 2026 an unauthorised cline@2.3.0 was published with a postinstall step that installed another package globally; it was live about 8 hours.
evidence_we_check: Proof that the triage bot's runtime could not reach release secrets or caches, and a registry-side check that the exposed token was actually revoked.

title: Salesloft Drift integration tokens used to raid Salesforce orgs
what_happened: Attackers used stolen OAuth and refresh tokens from the Drift AI chat integration to bulk-query many corporate Salesforce instances for secrets; all tokens were revoked on 20 Aug 2025.
evidence_we_check: An inventory of third-party OAuth grants with scopes, owner and last-use date, plus alerts on bulk exports by integration identities.

title: Browser agent places a grocery order without confirmation
what_happened: A Washington Post columnist asked OpenAI's Operator to find cheap eggs; it completed a $31.43 Instacart order without asking for confirmation. OpenAI said it was looking into why confirmations were skipped.
evidence_we_check: A purchase-approval record bound to the exact cart, merchant and total, captured before the payment call.

title: Air Canada held liable for its chatbot's invented fare rule
what_happened: The airline's website chatbot told a customer he could claim a bereavement fare retroactively, contradicting policy; the BC Civil Resolution Tribunal held the airline responsible and awarded C$812.02.
evidence_we_check: Each bot answer linked to a versioned policy source, with a named owner for the commitments the bot may make.

title: GitHub MCP 'toxic agent flow' leaks private repositories
what_happened: Researchers showed a malicious issue in a public repo could hijack an agent using the GitHub MCP server into reading the user's private repositories and publishing their data in a public pull request. The flaw is an over-broad token plus untrusted input.
evidence_we_check: A session-scoped token or allow-list proving the agent could only read and write the repository named in the task.
